course_title: Advanced Chinese to English Translation in the Age of AI
course_description:
This course builds on the translation concepts introduced in CHIN2700 and extends their application to texts of both the same and new, more complex, genre. In so doing, an advanced understanding of genre-specific issues in translation from Chinese into English is provided as well as advanced development of context-appropriate English expression.

The courseﾠis divided intoﾠmodules designed to give students training in the translation of different genres including texts drawn from areas such as politics, history, science, government, amongst others. Students will be guided inﾠtranslation skills required for Chinese>English translation of the texts under study; translation issues relating to each genre; and specific translation issues raised by texts under study. Students will also be guided in the production of a linguistically and culturally appropriate translation of the source text, in a way that provides students with an understanding ofﾠNAATI professional expectations.

assessment_details.title: In-class presentation
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Time limited, Peer assessed, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: In-Class Oral Presentation (35%) Timing: Weeks 11–12 Format: 5-minute timed presentation supported by one PowerPoint slide + palm cards Prepare a presentation reflecting on a given translation task and deliver it in class. Students will have at least THREE weeks to prepare the presentation in advance. The presentation should critically analyse the translation process and demonstrate students' understanding of the source text as well as challenges and strategies involved in the translation process. During the presentation, students are NOT permitted to read from a prepared transcript; however, students may refer to palm cards occasionally to support their delivery. The presentation should address the following areas: An accurate understanding of the Source Text (ST): Provide a brief overview of the source text and discuss its key linguistic, cultural, stylistic, or contextual features. Easy and difficult aspects of the translation task: Identify elements that were straightforward to translate and explain words/sentences that make the translation work challenging. Translation strategies used: Discuss the translation methods and strategies (including any AI tool) you have applied to address specific issues and achieve an effective translation. Reflection: Reflect on what you have learned from completing the translation task, including any skills, insights, technology or knowledge gained from the translation practice. Presentation: 30% + Peer Assessment: 5% Students will be assessed on the clarity of their analysis, the relevance and effectiveness of the translation strategies discussed, the depth of their reflection, and their ability to communicate their ideas effectively within the allocated time limit. AI and MT Statement This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. assessment_details.title: Final Exam (Online - Blackboard Ultra)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The final exam consists of multiple choice questions and a text for translation revision, testing students' knowledge and skills developed from all the weeks. The text for translation revision will represent the different genres studied in this course. Students may have access to lecture notes and paper dictionaries during the exam. The exam is online on Blackboard (Ultra). Be sure to access a reliable internet connection. You will have 60 minutes of working time plus 10 minutes for planning. Your time begins once you start the exam, and it must be completed in ONE attempt. You may use any printed materials or online tools to complete this assessment, but you must demonstrate your independent thinking and understanding of translation and getting help from other people is strictly prohibited. Auto submission is set in the system. AI and MT Statement This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description
